raw_response:
I have been doing this 45 years. My man and me work 33 mu. No children here to help, so we do what we can and hire a little help at busy times.

I do like everyone in our village does. The good land we plant wheat in winter, then maize after the wheat comes off in summer — same ground, two crops. That is 20 mu. The other 13 mu I put in cotton because cotton likes the sandier piece and we have grown cotton there for many years.

For fertilizer I buy what the shop in town sells, same as my neighbors. For wheat I put two bags of the compound (that is 100 jin, 50 kg) per mu before I plough, and then I top-dress with one bag of urea when it greens up in spring — that is about half a bag, 25 jin per mu. My neighbor Old Wang did less one year and his wheat was yellow and thin, so I do not cut back. Better to spend the money than see a bad harvest.

For maize after wheat, I put urea twice — once at knee-high, once when the tassel comes. Maize here does well, 1000 jin per mu is normal.

For cotton I put more fertilizer because cotton eats a lot. I also spray many times — cotton bugs are bad, bollworm and aphid. I spray whenever I see bugs, maybe six times in a season. This is what everyone does or you lose the bolls.

Seeds I buy from the dealer, the improved kind — the old seeds nobody sells anymore. Plough-man comes with the rotary machine, 40 yuan a mu, everyone uses him.

Irrigation — we have a well. Wheat I water three or four times: after planting, in spring when it greens up, at jointing, and when the grain fills. Maize one or two waters if the rain is short. Cotton two or three waters.
